concepts.why: The presence of a heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components in the left maxillary sinus, along with the displacement of the inferior rectus muscle and the absence of cytologic atypia, suggests a diagnosis of Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma.

The erosion of the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells by the mass, along with the presence of a spindle cell process, suggests a diagnosis of Maxillary Sinus Tumor.
The presence of mild left-sided proptosis and the displacement of the inferior rectus muscle suggests a diagnosis of Orbital Tumor.
